steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Stir flour, sugar, cornmeal, baking powder, and salt together in a mixing bowl. Pour in milk, beaten eggs, vegetable oil, melted butter, and honey; stir just to moisten.
Pour batter into the prepared baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean, about 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Sweet Cornbread Cake
raw_recipe.description: This sweet, moist cornbread is made with cornmeal, honey, eggs, melted butter, and whole milk; simply irresistible served hot from the oven.
raw_recipe.name: Sweet Cornbread Cake

review.reviewBody: Very nice. No vegetable oil because I used most of it to fry chicken, so I used all butter. I also used buttermilk. Even when I cut the recipe in half, it baked up beautifully. Thirty minutes and wa-la, perfect. No issues with sinking bread when you thought it was done. And the flavor is very fluffy and sweet. My kids and husband especially liked this. I served it with whipped butter and extra honey. Thank you for sharing your recipe. NOTE: I served this with Tanya's Louisiana Southern Fried Chicken and Broccoli Salad. It was a nice comforting dinner. EDITED: I've made this three times now, in 24 hours. My family has dubbed this the best cornbread they've ever had.

This cornbread is one of the best on the site! It rivals "Grandmother's Buttermilk Cornbread" 'til now I thought that was my favorite. I cut the recipe in half and used one up of cornmeal and one cup of flour. It was perfectly done in 38 minutes - moist and delicous. I think the only thing that could possibly make this better would be to replace the whole milk with buttermilk.

I used Bob's Red Mill Gluten Free 1 to 1 Baking flour and Califia unsweetened almond milk. I used a 9"x9" Pyrex dish and baked it an extra 15 minutes. It came out looking, smelling and tasting amazing! This cornbread is very sweet and cake-like.

This recipe IS awesome! The ONLY changes I made was with the honey, and milk. I FORGOT to add the honey to the mixture, so I made honey butter instead, and brushed it over the hot cornbread as soon as it came out of the oven. I subbed b'milk instead of regular milk. The cornbread was so moist, and it baked up nice and soft. I also baked this in a 10 in cast iron skillet. I ate this with a basic chili recipe on a rainy, and cold day.. The few leftover slices we had? I nuked my portion of cornbread in the microwave for about 30 seconds...Mmmmm hmmmmm!!! Tasted like it was just made! I'm a southern girl, and this is not my usual way of making cornbread, NEVERTHELESS, it's a cornbread CAKE, and I really enjoyed this one, and so did my fiance... a nice change from the norm! This WILL be MY go to when I want to break tradition and do something different with my cornbread! Thanks for sharing! Peace and blessings!

I didn't have regular corn meal, so I used 4 cups of corn flour and it came out great! Also, I don't have the patience to wait 45 minutes, so I used muffin top pans and they were ready in 12 minutes. So yummy, sweet and cakey, great with stewed apples! This is a huge recipe, it made 17 muffin tops and a dozen muffins, but they were all gone in a few hours!

Feels heavy because it's so moist but it's light, airy and rich! I added a can of niblets corn, drained. Because I had a bit of extra batter than my pan would hold I lined a muffin tin pan with paper liners and tried the batter as muffins too, knowing they would need only 12 - 18 minutes to cook instead of 45 minutes. Both the corn bread cooked in the 9 x 13 pan and the corn bread muffins were delicious! My husband likes the idea of corn bread muffins in his lunchbox for snacking. Guess I'll make a bigger batch of muffins and maybe a small loaf with the rest of the batter!

It's snowing here so I had planned to make cornbread and chowder. We are almost out of milk so I got creative. I had a bunch of very ripe bananas so I used all the dry ingredients and mixed 2 cups water with 4 ripe bananas and a mixture of oil/melted butter to equal a cup. I didn't add the honey because the bananas made it sweet. It was supposed to be a breakfast bread in the morning, and luckily, there is still some left for tomorrow, because we had it for dessert. So moist. The point being that use what you have and adapt. Breads are versatile and breakfast breads are a treat.
I used half and half, buttermilk, and whole milk. I added 1/2 teaspoon baking soda , and baked it in a bundt cake pan. We had the cake with fresh sliced peaches.

We have used this cornbread recipe for several years now. People ask for it regularly and light up when they try it. The only reason I rate it a 4 instead of 5 is because I find it to be too sweet as written. I use a 1/4 c of white sugar and a 1/4 c of brown sugar to add a little depth and lessen the sweetness a bit. Of course, that's personal preference anyway. Otherwise, this one is perfect for us. Moist, tender, and forgiving - a little more or less of the baking powder, oil, butter isn't going to ruin this. It also halves or doubles very easily. I've made in larger and smaller baking dishes and in cast iron skillets, all with good results. It makes a lovely tamale pie (we like the cornbread on the bottom!) and we have also added things like jalapeno & cheddar or sausage & sage/poultry seasoning & apple. We're going to try creole shrimp and buttery broth sometime, kind of like we like polenta. Slicing it in half and grilling the cut side in the cast skillet with butter makes a nice simple breakfast topped with a fried egg. Thanks a lot for the recipe. It has been well-used.
Baked at 5,300 ft above sea level. I decreased the sugar to 1 cup and increased temp to 360 F. Baked for 40 minutes. Came out super moist and golden light brown on top.
My go to cornbread recipe. It works well with dairy free milk and 1:1 Gluten Free flour mix
I add some shredded cheddar and Monterey Jack cheese Plus jalapeños. Yummy yummy yum yum
Made it for the first time and it was really good. Have not made cornbread in years and I felt good about it. Gonna make some chili later today to go with it. Try it.
I think it needed more cornmeal in it.

This is dangerously delicious ! If I make it as a side for chili I end up eating the whole thing (not at one sitting 😅) It is cake-y and not as dense as some other recipes but I think that’s what I like about it. I’ve also made this in tiny cupcake size for a party and they were a hit! The small size had more crunchy outsides and turned out not as fluffy but they were still super tasty 😋 I may experiment with adding some jalapeños next time. Enjoy!
I subbed gluten-free flour and non-dairy milk. It came out absolutely perfect. A definite keeper for me!
I increased the cornmeal by 1 cup and decreased the flour by 1 cup, also substituted 1/3 cup of the oil with 1/3 cup of applesauce. delicious.
The best! My family loves it! I will never make any other way!
I have been searching for a great recipe using cornmeal. Not one cornmeal muffin or cake recipe I have come across has turned out great let alone tasted great. But this. Totally a winner! So good!!!
Delicious as is! Moist with a tender crumb! Sometimes for non holidays, I cut the sugar in half. Great recipe! Family loves it!
